Leverandøren skal ha nødvendig kapasitet, kompetanse og tydelige rutinebeskrivelser for å ivareta alle Trondheim kommunes innfordringsområder, herunder blant annet kommunale eiendomsavgifter, kommunal husleie og annen restanse, parkering, startlån, sosiallån, UMS og for mye utbetalt lønn.Viser til konkurransedokumentene for ytterligere detaljer.

title: precisionFDA cloud-based genomics platform
description: SPECIAL NOTICE � INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Office of Acquisitions and Grants Services (OAGS) Acquisition Title: FY26�FY30 precisionFDA Platform Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Acquisition Identification Number: ODT-2026-132021 NAICS Code: 541714 PSC Code: D319 (Cloud Computing) Set-Aside: Small Business (DNAnexus confirmed SB under NAICS 541714) Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price IDIQ Period of Performance: 08/10/2026 � 08/09/2030 Estimated Value: $33,000,000 Notice: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Office of Digital Transformation (ODT), Office of Data Analytics and Research (ODAR), Health Informatics Staff (HIS), intends to award a sole-source Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to: DNAnexus, Inc. 1975 West El Camino Real, Suite 204 Mountain View, CA 94040 This action is being conducted under the authority of FAR 6.302-1 (Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements), pursuant to 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1). Description of Requirement: The FDA requires continued operations, sustainment, modernization, and cloud support for the precisionFDA platform � a FISMA-authorized, secure, cloud-based collaborative research environment for next-generation sequencing (NGS) assay evaluation, genomics and multi-omics research, and regulatory science applications. The platform supports collaboration between FDA researchers and reviewers, as well as external collaborators and sponsors across multiple FDA centers, including CDER, CBER, CDRH, CVM, and CFSAN. Services to be acquired include: Platform access licenses, cloud computing resources (compute, storage, data transfer on AWS), operations and maintenance, security patching, and technical support Continuation of all current precisionFDA capabilities, including immutable files with chain of provenance, file locking, Government-only spaces, Protected spaces, Review spaces, FHIR Stations, Scientific Challenge Framework, and custom data portal development capability Development and maintenance of the precisionFDA High (FISMA High) platform on FDA GovCloud FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) and FISMA High compliance maintenance per NIST SP 800-53 Rev5 Integration support for FDA enterprise systems including the Global Substance Registration System (GSRS) Training, user support, disaster recovery, and business continuity services Place of Performance: Contractor facility and FDA White Oak Campus, 10903 New Hampshire Avenue, Silver Spring, MD 20993 Basis for Sole Source Determination: Comprehensive market research was conducted in accordance with FAR Part 10, evaluating 20 vendors with a detailed assessment of 8 shortlisted vendors against 33 critical capability requirements. The research conclusively determined that DNAnexus is the only vendor capable of meeting FDA's requirements for Day-1 continuity of the precisionFDA mission on the date of contract award, for the following reasons: Only vendor with zero capability gaps: DNAnexus is the only vendor that scored fully across all 33 assessed capabilities. No alternative vendor can replicate on Day 1 the precisionFDA capabilities of immutable files with chain of provenance, file locking, Government-only spaces, Protected spaces, Review spaces, FHIR Stations, the Scientific Challenge Framework, or custom data portal development capability. Unique secure external collaboration capability: DNAnexus is the only platform provider able to facilitate secure FDA-sponsored scientific challenges and controlled communication with industry sponsors, vendors, academic researchers, and international regulatory partners while maintaining regulatory-grade confidentiality controls, data segregation, audit trails, and compliance features. Institutional knowledge and validated workflows: FDA has invested over seven years in developing, validating, and documenting bioinformatics workflows on the precisionFDA platform. Over 300 FDA scientific reviewers, bioinformaticians, and research scientists have been trained on the platform. The application library includes 100+ versioned apps. Migration to an alternative platform would require complete revalidation and an estimated $14.7M full rebuild. FedRAMP and FISMA compliance: DNAnexus holds FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) authorization (Cert ID FR1814557199, confirmed June 18, 2026) and FISMA Moderate ATO (FDA-sponsored). DNAnexus is actively enrolled in the PRISM High-Impact Platform Pilot (March 2026) providing a structured pathway to FedRAMP High authorization, with a parallel FISMA High ATO track to support the precisionFDA High platform. Small Business: DNAnexus is confirmed as a Small Business under NAICS 541714 (~277 employees; 1,000-employee size standard). Response Instructions: This notice is not a solicitation and does not commit the Government to award a contract. No award will be made solely on the basis of responses to this notice. Interested parties who believe they are capable of meeting the Government's requirements in their entirety may submit a written capability statement to the Contracting Officer no later than 15 calendar days from the date of this notice. Capability statements will be evaluated to determine whether full and open competition should be conducted in lieu of a sole-source award. Capability statements must address, at a minimum, the vendor's ability to provide Day-1 continuity of all current precisionFDA capabilities, FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) authorization status, and a demonstrated pathway to FISMA High authorization. Responses must be submitted electronically to: Steven Gagnon, Contracting Officer Email: Steven.Gagnon@fda.hhs.gov Allison Meads, Contract Specialist Email: Allison.Meads@fda.hhs.gov Subject Line: Capability Statement � precisionFDA IDIQ Sole Source Notice, ODT-2026-132021 Telephone responses will not be accepted. The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred in preparing a response to this notice. description: The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) is conducting a market survey to identify potential sources for a series of anticipated contracts/task order awards capable of providing Technical Support Services for the FHWA Office of Safety and Operations Research & Development (HRSO) located at the Turner-Fairbank Highway Research Center (TFHRC) in McLean, VA. title: Languages Testing for Interpreters
description: Services Requirement This requirement is for: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada Title: 20260726-IRB – Language Testing for Interpreters Description of the Requirement: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada has a requirement for service of testing components and test assessments for the recruitment of their interpreter contractors to Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB). Interpreter Services Contractors (ISCs) accredited by the IRB must successfully complete three (3) language tests with a minimum score of 70% to qualify for a contract: • Official Languages Test: Assesses the applicant’s ability to communicate in English or French. This is the first test administered, consisting of a short 15-minute written assessment designed to evaluate comprehension in one of the official languages. • Hearing Simulation (Oral) Test: Evaluates the applicant’s ability to perform consecutive interpretation between an official language and a target language, and vice versa. These tests are currently available in sixty (60) languages. However, there are only two versions of each language test, and the quality and consistency of the tests vary. • Sight Translation Test: Measures the applicant’s ability to translate short documents similar to those that may be presented in a hearing room from the language of interpretation to English or French. This is the final test administered. Level of Security Requirement: Resource(s) Minimum Security Level Required is Reliability Status. Associated Documents: Request for Proposal (RFP) 20260726-IRB. Proposed period of contract: The proposed period of contract shall be from September 30, 2026, to March 31, 2027. The resulting contract will include three (3) one-year optional periods. Estimated Level of Effort: The overall annual cumulative estimated level of effort of the contract(s) will be for 300 tests. Multiple contracts: Considering that contract(s) will be issue based on offerors qualified language(s), this solicitation could results on multiples contracts. Contracting Authority: Steve Dessureault Phone Number: 514-249-2780 Email address: steve.dessureault@irb-cisr.gc.ca Note: Please address all inquiry questions to the Contracting Authority by email only.

title: Kegaska Harbour Service Area Development (Phase I)
description: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) invites bids for the construction of Phase I of the Service Area Development Project at Kegaska Harbour, located on Quebec's Lower North Shore. The work generally consists of excavation and soil management, grading of existing areas, placement of fill materials to create new storage areas, paving of a portion of the service area, relocation of an existing crane, construction of concrete works, installation of barriers and safety guardrails, construction of an electrical building, civil and electrical works, installation of site lighting, and installation of conduits and infrastructure for future project phases. The Contractor shall coordinate the work with the Harbour Authority to maintain port operations and access to facilities throughout the project.

title: Alma Beach Parking Lot Reconstruction, Fundy National Park
description: 5P468-26-0214/A Alma Beach Parking Lot Reconstruction, Fundy National Park BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca . Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808 The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT The reconstruction of the Alma Beach parking lot located at the main entrance to Fundy National Park in Alma, New Brunswick. The work includes removal of the existing deteriorated pavement structure, excavation, installation of geotextile and granular base/subbase materials, new asphalt paving, replacement of a catch basin and storm sewer piping, replacement of selected concrete curbs and sidewalks and associated site works. All work must be completed Fall 2026. To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value between $500,001 > $ 1,000,000, Taxes extra. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI04 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than November 30, 2026 OPTIONAL SITE VISIT There will be an optional site visit on Thursday October 1st at 11:00 AM local time. Interested bidders are to meet at 8616 Main St, Alma, NB – Alma Beach Parking Lot, Fundy National Park Safety Attire: In order to be guaranteed access to the site visit all persons should have the proper personal protection equipment (safety glasses, footwear, vests and hard hats etc.). Contractor’s personnel/individuals who do not have the proper safety attire may be denied access to the site. Bidders are requested to communicate with the Contracting Authority no later than noon on Tuesday September 29, 2026 to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders may be requested to sign an attendance sheet. Bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative will not be given an alternative appointment but they will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than 5 business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Canada Student Financial Assistance (CSFA) Program - Request for Information (RFI)
description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) and Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC), collectively referred to as Canada, are initiating a procurement process for a service delivery contract for the administration of the Canada Student Financial Assistance Program (CSFA) Program. The CSFA Program aims to make post-secondary education more accessible by delivering financial assistance in a reliable, affordable, and client-focused manner. This Request for Information (RFI) provides: information about the RFI process and procurement priorities and timelines; a high-level overview of the current service delivery model and requirements; a description of key legislation and the importance of complying with government policies; considerations for the next service delivery contract; and a series of questions for interested suppliers to answer.

title: Q702--Gainesville OPC IOTA
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) August 13, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation Services in support of the Gainesville, FL OPC 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation (IOT&A) services for Gainesville, FL Outpatient Clinic (OPC). This requirement supports VHA's mission by providing contractor support services to help bring the hospital into full planned operations that will provide health care services to Veterans. This will be a firm-fixed-price contract with an estimated Period of Performance of 46-months. The North Florida/South Georgia Healthcare System has been approved for a major lease to create an expanded service opportunity for Veteran health care at Gainesville OPC Consolidation. This project proposes to lease a new outpatient clinic in Gainesville, FL. This project is approximately 188,418 net usable square foot (NUSF) in the vicinity of Gainesville, FL, including 1300 parking spaces. The clinic will expand on care currently provided at the existing contracted lease spaces and allow an expansion to the current footprint as well as added new for a decompression of the Malcom Randall VA Medical Center (VAMC) in Gainesville, FL. The lease would allow VA to consolidate outpatient services at one location for mental health, home based primary care, specialty care and ancillary diagnostics identified in the Strategic Capital Investment Planning (SCIP) process. The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project. The scope of services includes Comprehensive Project Management, Comprehensive Interior Design, FF&E, and Space Planning Support; CONOPS and Transitioning Planning; Acquisition Support Services to include package development, Activation, Delivery, Relocation and Installation, Training, and Turnover and Post Occupancy Support for the identified project. title: Procure for Bulk Cryogenics
description: General Information This is a solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)/Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12.201, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), located in Indian Head, Maryland, intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order using Simplified Acquisition Procedures to Procure for Bulk Cryogenics. Solicitation Details Quotes are being requested under Request for Quotations (RFQ) N0017426Q1118. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 325120 and the associated small business size standard is 1200 employees. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the FAR/RFO. This RFQ incorporates all provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) DPN 20260507. Basis for Award The Government will award a purchase order resulting from this solicitation to the responsible vendor whose quote conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The Government intends to evaluate all timely quotes received from eligible vendors on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. The Government intends to evaluate quotations and award a purchase order without discussion. Evaluation Factors: Technical: Quotes must reflect the required specifications and the exact brand specified in the Statement of Work. Price: Quotes must include all applicable costs, including shipping and handling. Questions and Clarifications Questions regarding this requirement must be submitted via email to latrice.t.whitfield.civ@us.navy.mil no later than September 25, 2026. All answers will be provided by October 5th, 2026. Submission Instructions Quote packages are due by October 15, 2026, at 10:00 AM EST. Late quotes will not be considered. Quote packages shall be sent via email to latrice.t.whitfield.civ@us.navy.mil and must contain a cover sheet that provides the following information: Official Company Name; Point of Contact (including name, email address, and phone number); and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code.

SYNOPSIS AND REGULATORY PURPOSE This Sources Sought is published by the Mission and Installation Contracting Command Fort Stewart in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 10 (Market Research) and Part 19 (Small Business Programs). title: Large Area Display System (LADS)
description: Sources Sought Notice Number: H9224126S61892 The Technology Application Program Office (TAPO) is conducting market research to identify potential vendors capable of responding to the requirements described below. This is a Sources Sought Notice issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), nor does it oblige the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this request, so quotes will not be considered. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this synopsis or any follow-up information requests. Response is strictly voluntary; it is not mandatory to submit a response to this notice to participate in any formal RFP process that may take place in the future. However, it should be noted that information gathered through this notice may significantly influence the Government�s acquisition strategy. All interested parties will be required to respond separately to any solicitations posted as a result of this sources sought notice. Requirements: The Government seeks to identify potential sources with aircraft Large Area Display System (LADS) for military rotary wing Air Vehicle Systems (AVS) that are commercial products. These airborne avionics grade display system will serve as the primary human machine interface for pilotage and situational awareness tasks by the aircrew. Safety-critical video processing and control are expected to reside externally to the LADS. The Government is interested in a display subsystem capable of deterministic, bounded-latency presentation of video and symbology as an endpoint within an existing Cockpit Display System architecture. The system must be designed with a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) to ensure interoperability, reusability, and future growth. Attributes of interest are Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP), environmental and electromagnetic susceptibility characteristics, and display characteristics. Further details are available to potential sources that the Joint Certification Program (JCP) have certified as eligible for access to unclassified, non-public military technical data and have a current JCP approved DD Form 2345, Military Critical Technical Data Agreement. Key Information: NAICS Code: 334511 (Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing). Interested sources may recommend other NAICS Codes for consideration. Small Business Size Standard: The small business size standard is 1,350 employees. PSC: 1680 - Miscellaneous aircraft accessories and components. Response Requested: Interested parties are invited to submit a capabilities statement (on company letterhead) demonstrating their qualifications, capabilities and experience in providing the requirement. Responses should be no longer than 10 pages and include the following: 1. Source Profile: A. Company Name and Address B. Affiliate Information (parent companies, joint ventures, potential teaming partners) C. Year Established & Number of Employees D. Two Points of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email) E. Unique Entity ID and CAGE Code (as registered in SAM: http://www.sam.gov/) F. Business Size & Designation (must correlate with SAM registration) 2. Technical Capability Describe the LADS offered relative to the requirement above, to include display size and resolution, luminance range and night vision imaging system compatibility, SWaP characteristics, video and symbology interfaces supported, and qualification and certification status. 3. Commercial Product Status A. Whether the LADS is of a type customarily used by non-governmental entities for other than governmental purposes, and whether it has been sold, leased, or licensed, or offered for sale, lease, or license, to the general public. B. FAA Technical Standard Order authorization, if any (TSO number and revision). C. Rotary wing installations under a Type Certificate or Supplemental Type Certificate, if any (TC/STC number, aircraft make and model, approximate units fielded). 4. Small Business Considerations A. Whether the respondent is the manufacturer of the LADS. If not, ability to comply with the nonmanufacturer rule. B. Ability to comply with the applicable limitation on subcontracting. 5. Administrative Current SPRS Basic Assessment score and date; current CMMC level and assessment type; foreign ownership, control, or influence status. Submission Details: Deadline: 09 October 2026, 11:00 A.M. Eastern Time Email: Responses are to be submitted via email to Dr. Petrina Stack petrina.v.stack.civ@socom.mil and Chiffon Bradshaw chiffon.m.bradshaw.civ@socom.mil Submit in PDF. title: Gestione globale del centro socio assistenziale San Michele di Entracque.
description: L’appalto ha per oggetto l’affidamento del servizio di gestione della struttura per anziani denominata “Centro socio assistenziale San Michele”, che costituisce la parte preponderante del contratto, oltre ai seguenti servizi integrativi: – fornitura del servizio infermieristico alla popolazione residente; – fornitura di bagni protetti agli anziani richiedenti; – fornitura di pasti da erogare a domicilio agli anziani richiedenti; – fornitura di pasti da erogare agli utenti della mensa scolastica comunale; – assistenza agli alunni trasportati sullo scuolabus comunale; – assistenza agli alunni frequentanti la mensa scolastica comunale; – pulizia locali indicati dal Comune, ambulatorio infermieristico; – servizi aggiuntivi a richiesta e discrezione del Comune. Il Centro socio assistenziale “San Michele” è una struttura di proprietà comunale, sita a Entracque in via Ospedale n. 72, nel centro del paese, ubicata in un edificio storico, un tempo utilizzato come Ospedale di carità e Ospizio. La sede è stata oggetto di ristrutturazione edilizia, di riqualificazione e di efficientamento energetico negli anni 2024-2026. La struttura, che permette un’ospitalità permanente, risulta in possesso delle autorizzazioni necessarie al funzionamento finalizzato alla “Progettazione ed erogazione di servizi socio-sanitari ed assistenziali rivolti ad anziani autosufficienti e non autosufficienti in regime di residenzialità”. Le caratteristiche della struttura e della gestione sono specificate nel progetto per l'affidamento della gestione globale del centro socio assistenziale "San Michele" approvato con deliberazione di Giunta del Comune di Entracque n. 52 del 24/06/2026; con deliberazione di Giunta del Comune di Entracque n. 64 del 26/08/2026 è stata invece approvata la versione aggiornata del quadro economico.

title: Sources Sought - SLDA NCSO
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice for market research purposes only to identify capable firms for on-site Nuclear Criticality Safety (NCS) support for the Shallow Land Disposal Area (SLDA) environmental-remediation project in Parks Township, Armstrong County, Pennsylvania. This is a special notice only. No proposals are being requested or accepted in response to this notice. All responses must be submitted electronically through the designated Market Survey Form. 1. Description of Work The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Buffalo District, is seeking capability statements from qualified firms to determine the availability and technical capability of firms able to provide independent on-site nuclear criticality safety support for the Formerly Utilized Sites Remedial Action Program (FUSRAP) SLDA project. The anticipated requirement is a firm-fixed-price service contract with cost-reimbursable travel, consisting of a one-year base period and four option years. The contractor will provide a qualified primary NCS Officer and alternate NCS Officer to support active environmental-remediation operations at the SLDA site. The contractor will serve as an independent technical advisor to USACE and will provide oversight and quality assurance of the remediation contractor�s NCS program. The anticipated scope includes: Providing on-site presence during active remediation operations. Conducting field walkdowns and direct observation of remediation activities. Reviewing Nuclear Criticality Safety Evaluations, calculations, technical-basis documents, work plans, procedures, and other submittals. Assessing the implementation and effectiveness of criticality-safety controls. Conducting audits, assessments, and surveillance of the remediation contractor�s NCS program. Reviewing safety, radiological, operational, and nuclear quality-assurance documentation. Supporting the safe handling, measurement, processing, storage, transport, and disposal of excavated radiological materials, including special nuclear material. Preparing independent technical reports identifying findings, risks, and recommended corrective actions. Supporting coordination with USACE, the site owner, regulators, and other project stakeholders, as required. The work will primarily occur at the SLDA site in Parks Township, Pennsylvania. The requirement may also include periodic travel to USACE offices and other off-site meeting locations. 2. Submission Requirements & Instructions The only authorized method for submitting responses to this Sources Sought Notice is through the electronic Market Survey Form linked below. Responses submitted by email or any other method will not be accepted. Please limit responses to the specific information requested in the online form. Firms should be prepared to address their relevant experience, availability of qualified primary and alternate personnel, experience with nuclear criticality safety and radiological or HTRW remediation, and potential interest in serving as a prime contractor or teaming partner. Please limit your responses to the specific information requested within the online form. https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/CKsStcvvq4 https://forms.osi.apps.mil/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=unZN_HzxUEy5p48xY9J1gqWCk0sPU9lLvnwyNUMYjIlUMkxGQklYOTZHN0hKQUdBT0pGWjE3WDZCUi4u 3. Points of Contact For general inquiries, clarifications, or technical issues regarding the submission form, please contact the following representatives. Note: Do not email capability statements or survey responses to these addresses. Nathaniel M. Dent - Contract Specialist Nathaniel.m.dent@usace.army.mil Jeffrey G. Ernest - Contracting Officer Jeffrey.G.Ernest@usace.army.mil

The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation or award a contract as a result of this notice. AGENCY INFORMATION Department of the Interior National Park Service Contracting Operations (ConOps) East Point of Contact: Edward Dingle, Jr. Edward_dingle@ios.doi.gov 3. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Department of the Interior, National Park Service (NPS), is conducting market research to determine the availability and capability of qualified construction contractors to perform the Atrium Replacement at the Chickamauga Visitor Center, Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia, Project CHCH 315696. The contemplated project generally consists of replacement of the existing Visitor Center atrium, limited parking-lot modifications, reconfiguration of the north and south plazas, and associated fire-protection, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, communications, fire-alarm, architectural, structural, civil/site, and landscape improvements. The work is anticipated to be performed under a single prime construction contract and includes multiple interdependent construction disciplines requiring significant coordination by the prime contractor. Major elements of work include, but are not necessarily limited to: � Selective demolition and demolition of the existing Visitor Center atrium. � Construction of the replacement atrium, including structural, architectural, roofing, building-envelope, curtain-wall/glazing, entrance, and interior-finish work. � Civil, landscape, parking, pedestrian pathway, paving, grading, earthwork, stormwater, and related site improvements. � Fire-protection modifications, including dry-pipe sprinkler-system work. � Plumbing and facility drainage improvements. � HVAC/mechanical modifications, including associated piping, ductwork, equipment, controls, supports, vibration/seismic requirements, and testing and balancing. � Electrical modifications, including demolition, conductors, raceways, grounding, panelboards, wiring devices, lighting, and associated electrical distribution work. � Fire-alarm, communications, and related life-safety systems. � Temporary facilities and controls, environmental protection, construction waste management, testing, commissioning, project documentation, and closeout. The specifications separately identify contract line items covering site demolition, demolition of the existing Visitor Center atrium, civil and landscape improvements, construction of the new atrium, fire-sprinkler upgrades, plumbing/drainage upgrades, mechanical improvements, and electrical improvements. Occupied Facility and Public Access The work will occur at an active National Park Service visitor facility. Areas outside the construction limits are expected to remain occupied by NPS personnel and accessible to park visitors. Construction activities must therefore be planned and coordinated to protect employees and the public, maintain access and required exits, and minimize disruption to park and Visitor Center operations. Temporary construction controls include fencing, barriers, and separation of construction activities from occupied/public areas. The project also contains requirements concerning historic-preservation treatment, protection of existing resources, ground-disturbing activities, construction scheduling, quality control, environmental protection, fire/life-safety continuity, and multidisciplinary construction coordination. Accordingly, the Government is particularly interested in determining whether firms�especially qualified small businesses�possess the experience, personnel, subcontractor resources, bonding capacity, and management systems necessary to serve as the prime contractor and integrator for the complete multidisciplinary requirement. 4. title: Rockaway Contract 3, ADA Cross Over, Queens County, New York
description: Pre-Solicitation NoticeThe New York District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (District) is preparing plans and specifications for construction of the Rockaway Contract 3 ADA cross over. DESCRIPTION: The East Rockaway Inlet to Rockaway Inlet (or Rockaway) project area is in the Borough of Queens, New York City. The Atlantic Oceanfront shoreline, which is a peninsula approximately 10 miles in length, generally referred to as the Rockaways, separates the Atlantic Ocean from Jamaica Bay immediately to the north. This project, Rockaway Contract 3, includes the following: nine elevated, timber, pedestrian crossover structures that will provide ADA access to the beach, sand fence and dune vegetation will be added to the localized areas of the ADA structures. The nine ADA elevated timber crossovers are located at Beach 147th, 142nd, 135th, 131st, 67th, 44th, 17th, 13th and 11th streets. The span of the truss deck is approximately 44 feet over the crest of the dune and has landward and seaward ramps varying in length. There are also options for aluminum railings and handrails and reinforced plastic lumber decking, as well as options to remove 19 timber groins. Award is projected in November/December 2026. Estimated project duration is 18 months about 550 calendar days. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990 (Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction).LOCATION: The project area is in the Borough of Queens, New York City.Construction cost is in the range of $10,000,000 to $25,000,000.

title: Market Survey - Microgrid - United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne
description: A market survey is being conducted to determine if there are a reasonable number of interested businesses for the below future project. If your firm is an Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZone, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business and you are interested in this project please respond appropriately. Project Location: United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne Project Description: This is a Design/Bid/Build project. The US Government intends to solicit to construction firms to perform military construction and other Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (SRM) projects in the country of Germany as described within this announcement for the state of Bavaria. Construct a fully functional, islandable, and black start capable microgrid. The microgrid will include solar photovoltaic (PV) power production to provide daily, on-site renewable energy generation to offset incoming power from the local utility. Additionally, this project will also include diesel fuel generators, a battery energy storage system (BESS), and a microgrid controller to control all energy generation assets and manage electrical loads. This microgrid system will connect and distribute power on a government owned electrical distribution system. This microgrid is to provide resilient power to facilities at Katterbach/Bismarck Kaserne. Contract duration is estimated at 743 calendar days. The estimated cost range is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. NAICS code is 237130. All interested Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZONE, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business contractors should respond to this survey via the form link or QR code provided on this posting by Friday, October 09, 2026 by 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Responses should include: Identification and verification of the company�s size status. Contractor�s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code(s). Identification of firm�s current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. Description of Experience � Provide descriptions on up to three (3) projects completed by you as the prime contractor or if the offeror is a Small Business, they can provide Past Performance of affiliates in accordance with DFARS 215.305(a)(2)(C). Submissions of Past Performance from affiliates shall include documentation of the affiliation to the offeror. To be relevant, the projects submitted should be greater than 95% construction complete or completed within the last five (5) years and are similar to this project in scope and complexity. Demonstrate experience including self-performing 15% of the construction. Provide documentation demonstrating experience for projects of similar type projects. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages and quality of performance. Projects similar in scope shall include construction of a microgrid demonstrating a sufficient combination of the following scope elements to substantiate the offeror's technical competency, based on the complexity, scale, and integration of the demonstrated elements: (1) Installation of diesel centralized generators to power multiple buildings and fuel tank farm system (2) Installation of necessary breakers and switchgears (3) Installation of photovoltaic systems (4) Installation of electrical and telecommunication duct bank (5) Installation of a BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) (6) Information and communication systems (7)Commissioning of microgrid systems Projects similar in size to this project include: Construction of microgrid systems that meet or exceed the following: (1) Construction and installation of diesel generators able to handle loads of .5 to 2.5MW (2) Construction and installation of a PV Array of power production of 500 kW to 1.5 MW (3) Construction and installation of a BESS of 2 MWh to 10 MWh Based on definitions above, for each project submitted include: (1) Current percentage of construction complete and the date when it was or will be completed. (2) Size of the project (3) Scope of the project (4) The dollar value of the construction contract (5) The percentage of work that was self-performed as project and/or construction management services or physical construction type work. (6) Whether the project was design build or design/bid/build (7) Identify the number of subcontractors by construction trade utilized for each project. 5. title: GEN6 V006 CYBER SCAN
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Patuxent River, MD intends to negotiate and award a Delivery Order under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N0042126G1005 with Collins Aerospace (CA), 400 Collins Road NE, Cedar Rapids, IA 52498-0505 to provide Naval Air Systems Command, Air Combat Electronics Program Office (PMA209) with the GEN6 V006 Cyber Scan in support of the AN/ARC-210(V) RT-2036(C) v006, hereinafter referred to as Gen6. This effort consists of the following elements: Develop one (1) beta software scan of the Gen6 v006. Develop one (1) final software scan of the Gen6 v006. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C 2304(c)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 6.103-2, �only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.� The AN/ARC-210(V) electronic protection (EP) radio systems and associated support equipment have been determined to be commercial products and CA will not provide or sell the technical data necessary to procure the items competitively or provide support for these products. Therefore, CA is the only responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. The Government does not intend to fund the development or qualification of other sources for fulfilling this requirement. However, interested parties may identify their interest and capability by responding to this requirement. The Government will consider all information received prior to the closing date of this synopsis. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. No phone inquiries will be entertained. All inquiries and concerns shall be addressed via email to Grace Gillespie at grace.a.gillespie.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 09 October 2026, 2:00pm eastern time. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Companies interested in subcontracting opportunities should contact Collins Aerospace directly.

title: Microgrid - United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne
description: A market survey is being conducted to determine if there are a reasonable number of interested businesses for the below future project. If your firm is an Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZone, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business and you are interested in this project please respond appropriately. Project Location: United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne Project Description: This is a Design/Bid/Build project. The US Government intends to solicit to construction firms to perform military construction and other Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (SRM) projects in the country of Germany as described within this announcement for the state of Bavaria. Construct a fully functional, islandable, and black start capable microgrid. The microgrid will include solar photovoltaic (PV) power production to provide daily, on-site renewable energy generation to offset incoming power from the local utility. Additionally, this project will also include diesel fuel generators, a battery energy storage system (BESS), and a microgrid controller to control all energy generation assets and manage electrical loads. This microgrid system will connect and distribute power on a government owned electrical distribution system. This microgrid is to provide resilient power to facilities at Katterbach/Bismarck Kaserne. Contract duration is estimated at 743 calendar days. The estimated cost range is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. NAICS code is 237130. All interested Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZONE, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business contractors should respond to this survey via the form link or QR code provided on this posting by Friday, October 09, 2026 by 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Responses should include: Identification and verification of the company�s size status. Contractor�s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code(s). Identification of firm�s current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. Description of Experience � Provide descriptions on up to three (3) projects completed by you as the prime contractor or if the offeror is a Small Business, they can provide Past Performance of affiliates in accordance with DFARS 215.305(a)(2)(C). Submissions of Past Performance from affiliates shall include documentation of the affiliation to the offeror. To be relevant, the projects submitted should be greater than 95% construction complete or completed within the last five (5) years and are similar to this project in scope and complexity. Demonstrate experience including self-performing 15% of the construction. Provide documentation demonstrating experience for projects of similar type projects. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages and quality of performance. Projects similar in scope shall include construction of a microgrid demonstrating a majority of the following scope elements: (1) Installation of diesel centralized generators to power multiple buildings and fuel tank farm system (2) Installation of necessary breakers and switchgears (3) Installation of photovoltaic systems (4) Installation of electrical and telecommunication duct bank (5) Installation of a BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) (6) Information and communication systems (7)Commissioning of microgrid systems Projects similar in size to this project include: Construction of microgrid systems that meet or exceed the following: (1) Construction and installation of diesel generators able to handle loads of .5 to 2.5MW (2) Construction and installation of a PV Array of power production of 500 kW to 1.5 MW (3) Construction and installation of a BESS of 2 MWh to 10 MWh Based on definitions above, for each project submitted include: (1) Current percentage of construction complete and the date when it was or will be completed. (2) Size of the project (3) Scope of the project (4) The dollar value of the construction contract (5) The percentage of work that was self-performed as project and/or construction management services or physical construction type work. (6) Whether the project was design build or design/bid/build (7) Identify the number of subcontractors by construction trade utilized for each project. 5. Small Businesses are reminded under RFO 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting; they must perform at least 15% of the cost of the contract, not including the cost of materials, with the firm�s own employees for general construction-type procurement. Include the percentage of work that will be self-performed on this project, and how it will be accomplished. title: GLWACH Construct Hospital Parking and Renovate Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL)
description: W912DQ279A002 REQUEST FOR MARKET INFORMATION / NOTICE OF INDUSTRY WEBINAR FOR GENERAL LEONARD WOOD ARMY COMMUNITY HOSPTIAL (GLWACH) CONSTRUCT HOSPITAL PARKING AND RENOVATE OPTICAL FABRICATION LABORATORY (OFL) PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Kansas City District, is requesting market intelligence information to identify qualified industry partners capable of supporting a potential Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a for the stated General Leonard Wood Community Hospital (GLWACH) project at Fort Leonard Wood, MO. The Government is seeking industry feedback to better understand the commercial market interest, market capabilities, market capacity and innovative business practices that may inform the acquisition strategy and structure of the potential OT Agreement. This is not a Request for Qualifications. It does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award an agreement or reimburse respondents for costs associated with responding. Participation is voluntary. PROJECT OVERVIEW and REQUIREMENTS: Project Title: Hospital Parking Lot Construction and Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL) Renovation Location: Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri Agency: USACE, Kansas City District (NWK) NAICS Code: 236220-Commerical and Industrial Building Construction Planning and design activities are ongoing. The project�s phased funding profile is listed below: FY23: $31M (Expires September 30, 2027) FY29: $35M (Anticipated) The estimated magnitude for the entire overall effort is between $40 Million and $60M. The new General Leonard Wood Army Community Hospital requires the construction of new hospital parking lots, the renovation of an Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL), site work and infrastructure to support the newly constructed GLWACH. The parking lot construction includes site grading and drainage, vehicle circulation roads and parking, pedestrian sidewalks, landscaping (including the planting of trees), site lighting, wayfinding, and video surveillance. The contractor must always maintain 970 parking stalls during construction. The contractor must also ensure safe pedestrian access from the existing parking lots to the new hospital. A construction phasing plan and traffic management plan must be implemented to maintain a safe environment for hospital patrons and staff. The OFL renovation includes the demolition and replacement of the west wall at the current mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP) room, removing all equipment inside the MEP and capping all roof penetrations. After demolition the MEP space will remain and become additional storage space for the OFL contract. A new ADA (American with Disabilities Act) compliant entrance vestibule be provided on the west side of the building where the old connection to the hospital was. The OFL also includes the renovation of a medical supply warehouse. To meet life safety codes the optical fabrication lab (OFL) space on the lower level will receive a new egress corridor and lightning protection. The facility must remain fully operational during all deconstruction, demolition, and construction efforts. The former General Leonard Army Community Hospital and infrastructure must be decommissioned, dismantled, demolished, and removed prior to the construction of the new parking lot. This work included the decommissioning of a hospital and clinic, a central utility plant, abatement of hazardous materials and environmental liabilities. All existing paving, utilities, and other site appurtenances, including a helipad, must also be demolished and removed. Approximately 60,000 to 70,000 cubic yards of excavated soil will need to be cut and transported from an adjacent location to the project site for fill. POTENTIAL DELIVERY APPROACH: The Government is evaluating execution of this project using a Construction Manager At Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction Agreement authorized under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a with USACE as the Designer of Record (DOR). Using CMAR OT, the Government is particularly interested in commercial and collaborative practices to determine the following: Phasing and execution strategies to efficiently deliver the project Construction packaging and execution to optimize the given phased funding profile Early and continuous Government-industry collaboration; Collaborative design development and constructability; Contractor-Government open-book cost estimating and cost transparency; Collaborative project phasing and schedule certainty; Collaborative risk identification, mitigation and allocation; Innovation and alternative construction techniques; Overall cost, schedule, and mission outcomes. INDUSTRY INFORMATION REQUESTED: This request is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence regarding industry interest, capability and capacity, relevant experience using CMAR, open-book pricing, and potential commercial practices. The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding the use the same or similar collaborative commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this project using CMAR under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms should complete and submit: The attached Market Intelligence Questionnaire and A summary of their interest and capabilities to perform all the work identified for this project. The summary interest and capabilities is not a formal Request for Qualifications, and the response should not exceed 10 pages in length. The summary should also include the following information: The Company information (name, address, contact information, business structure) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code and/or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM.gov registration, if available. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Please submit the completed attached questionnaire and a summary of interest and capabilities via email to the individuals listed below no later than: 2:00 p.m. Central Time, 9 October 2026. Jeri L. Halterman at Jeri.l.halterman@usace.army.mil Courtesy copy: Dave Walsh at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. INDUSTRY WEBINAR: A virtual Industry Day to better explain the project requirements is scheduled prior to the requested date of submission, Wednesday, September 23, 2026, starting at 2:00 p.m. Central Daylight Time. Please email Jeri L. Halterman at Jeri.l.halterman@usace.army.mil and Dave Walsh at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil with your interest in attending the industry webinar. Early notification of interest will help us manage the appropriate network band-width necessary for 100% participation. title: GLWACH Construct Hospital Parking and Renovate Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL)
description: W912DQ279A002 REQUEST FOR MARKET INFORMATION / NOTICE OF INDUSTRY WEBINAR FOR GENERAL LEONARD WOOD ARMY COMMUNITY HOSPTIAL (GLWACH) CONSTRUCT HOSPITAL PARKING AND RENOVATE OPTICAL FABRICATION LABORATORY (OFL) PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Kansas City District, is requesting market intelligence information to identify qualified industry partners capable of supporting a potential Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a for the stated General Leonard Wood Community Hospital (GLWACH) project at Fort Leonard Wood, MO. The Government is seeking industry feedback to better understand the commercial market interest, market capabilities, market capacity and innovative business practices that may inform the acquisition strategy and structure of the potential OT Agreement. This is not a Request for Qualifications. It does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award an agreement or reimburse respondents for costs associated with responding. Participation is voluntary. PROJECT OVERVIEW and REQUIREMENTS: Project Title: Hospital Parking Lot Construction and Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL) Renovation Location: Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri Agency: USACE, Kansas City District (NWK) NAICS Code: 236220-Commerical and Industrial Building Construction Planning and design activities are ongoing. The project�s phased funding profile is listed below: FY23: $31M (Expires September 30, 2027) FY29: $35M (Anticipated) The estimated magnitude for the entire overall effort is between $40 Million and $60M. The new General Leonard Wood Army Community Hospital requires the construction of new hospital parking lots, the renovation of an Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL), site work and infrastructure to support the newly constructed GLWACH. The parking lot construction includes site grading and drainage, vehicle circulation roads and parking, pedestrian sidewalks, landscaping (including the planting of trees), site lighting, wayfinding, and video surveillance. The contractor must always maintain 970 parking stalls during construction. The contractor must also ensure safe pedestrian access from the existing parking lots to the new hospital. A construction phasing plan and traffic management plan must be implemented to maintain a safe environment for hospital patrons and staff. The OFL renovation includes the demolition and replacement of the west wall at the current mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP) room, removing all equipment inside the MEP and capping all roof penetrations. After demolition the MEP space will remain and become additional storage space for the OFL contract. A new ADA (American with Disabilities Act) compliant entrance vestibule be provided on the west side of the building where the old connection to the hospital was. The OFL also includes the renovation of a medical supply warehouse. To meet life safety codes the optical fabrication lab (OFL) space on the lower level will receive a new egress corridor and lightning protection. The facility must remain fully operational during all deconstruction, demolition, and construction efforts. The former General Leonard Army Community Hospital and infrastructure must be decommissioned, dismantled, demolished, and removed prior to the construction of the new parking lot. This work included the decommissioning of a hospital and clinic, a central utility plant, abatement of hazardous materials and environmental liabilities. All existing paving, utilities, and other site appurtenances, including a helipad, must also be demolished and removed. Approximately 60,000 to 70,000 cubic yards of excavated soil will need to be cut and transported from an adjacent location to the project site for fill. POTENTIAL DELIVERY APPROACH: The Government is evaluating execution of this project using a Construction Manager At Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction Agreement authorized under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a with USACE as the Designer of Record (DOR). Using CMAR OT, the Government is particularly interested in commercial and collaborative practices to determine the following: Phasing and execution strategies to efficiently deliver the project Construction packaging and execution to optimize the given phased funding profile Early and continuous Government-industry collaboration; Collaborative design development and constructability; Contractor-Government open-book cost estimating and cost transparency; Collaborative project phasing and schedule certainty; Collaborative risk identification, mitigation and allocation; Innovation and alternative construction techniques; Overall cost, schedule, and mission outcomes. INDUSTRY INFORMATION REQUESTED: This request is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence regarding industry interest, capability and capacity, relevant experience using CMAR, open-book pricing, and potential commercial practices. The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding the use the same or similar collaborative commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this project using CMAR under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms should complete and submit: The attached Market Intelligence Questionnaire and A summary of their interest and capabilities to perform all the work identified for this project. The summary interest and capabilities is not a formal Request for Qualifications, and the response should not exceed 10 pages in length. The summary should also include the following information: The Company information (name, address, contact information, business structure) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code and/or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM.gov registration, if available. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Please submit the completed attached questionnaire and a summary of interest and capabilities via email to the individuals listed below no later than: 2:00 p.m. Central Time, 9 October 2026. Jeri L. Halterman at Jeri.l.halterman@usace.army.mil Courtesy copy: Dave Walsh at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. INDUSTRY WEBINAR: A virtual Industry Day to better explain the project requirements is scheduled prior to the requested date of submission, Wednesday, September 23, 2026, starting at 2:00 p.m. Central Daylight Time. Please email Jeri L. Halterman at Jeri.l.halterman@usace.army.mil and Dave Walsh at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil with your interest in attending the industry webinar. Early notification of interest will help us manage the appropriate network band-width necessary for 100% participation. description: Air Combat Command's (ACC) mission requires robust Tactical Datalink (TDL) interoperability to improve mission effectiveness for United States Air Force (USAF), Joint, and coalition forces. To support this mission, the Government requires a modern software solution that serves as a relational database and analysis toolset. This toolset is essential for the iSMART (interoperable Systems Management and Requirements Transformation) process and is used to populate, edit, analyze, and manage TDL message data, platform implementations, and interoperability evaluations. The Contractor shall provide an existing commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software solution, including all necessary licenses, updates, training, and technical support. The software shall provide a comprehensive toolset for managing TDL platform specifications, conducting interoperability analysis, and supporting mission planning across the TDL enterprise. The TDL software solution must meet all requirements as listed in the Attachment 1 - Performance Work Statement.

title: Solicitation_S-280C/G Vehicle Mounted Shelter
description: ***10 SEP 2026 - AMD 0001 issued*** The Army Contracting Command - Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) is issuing this Request for Proposal (RFP) to establish a new five-year, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the manufacture and delivery of four (4) variants of the S-280C/G Vehicle Mounted Shelter. This is a non-commercial requirement. Requirement: The S-280C/G is a lightweight, tactical military shelter designed to house and protect sensitive electronic equipment and personnel. Manufacturing shall be in strict accordance with the Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) and ASTM E1975-22. The scope includes First Article Testing (FAT), production, and delivery of all associated technical and logistics data. National Stock Numbers (NSNs): 5411-01-304-3069 (Shielded) and 5411-01-092-0892 (Unshielded). Set-Aside: This is a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. The applicable size standard for NAICS 332311 is 750 employees. Award Basis: The Government intends to award a single IDIQ contract to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This will be a tradeoff source selection conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15. Contract Value: The minimum guaranteed value for this contract is $100,000.00. The maximum estimated contract ceiling is $4,000,000.00. Technical Data Package (TDP): The TDP for this solicitation is Export-Controlled (Distribution Statement C). To gain access, interested parties must have a current and valid DD Form 2345, "Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement" certification on file with the U.S./Canada Joint Certification Office (JCO). The TDP can be accessed through the attachments section of this announcement on SAM.gov by certified offerors. title: Z2DA--FY27 689-22-700 EHRM IU West Haven
description: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) is conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for the Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) Infrastructure Upgrades Construction project at the West Haven VA Medical Center (VAMC) located at 950 Campbell Avenue, West Haven CT 06516. INDUSTRY DAY: Please be advised that industry days have been scheduled for October 7, 2026 and October 8, 2026 in conjunction with this SSN. The posting can be found here (https://sam.gov/workspace/contract/opp/ea9ab14003ff4255aba63b8116c51901/view) or searching Electronic Health Record Modernization Construction Opportunities Notice ID: 36C776-27-AP-0151 at sam.gov. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Department of Veteran Affairs is in the process of migrating from its existing Computerized Patient Record System (CPRS) to the new EHRM platform. The scope of this project includes but is not limited to the following: upgrade facility fiber throughout the buildings to each Telecommunications Room (TR), provide a redundant fiber run throughout the facility to each TR, provide redundant fiber mains to the redundant demarcation rooms from the provider point, install data drops, install new electrical outlets throughout the facility, provide additional power in each TR, upgrade facility power distribution as required, upgrade facility HVAC distribution as required, physical security assessment and upgrades, and hazardous material abatement. In addition to ensuring adequate capacity for planned growth and maintenance, this project addresses deficiencies as defined by the PSRDM (Physical Security Design and Resiliency Manual) 2021 VA Standard. The following buildings have been identified as having deficiencies to address: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 11, 11A, 12, 14, 15, 16A, 21, 22, 24, 27, 34, 35, 35A, 36, 36A, 12A, 14A, 15A, 2B, and site. Project also includes new data center. title: HELICOPTER AERIAL SPRAYING IN NORTH DAKOTA
description: The contractor shall perform chemical application services on federal land administered by the USACE Garrison Project utilizing helicopter-based platforms. Services include 1) proactively surveying said lands for noxious weeds during appropriate growing season(s), 2) inventorying noxious weeds by collecting GPS data (coordinates, weed species, and acres of infestation), 3) controlling noxious weeds via appropriate helicopter chemical application capable of both spot treatment and solid coverage, 4) documenting chemical application services via submittal of completed pesticide application record (PAR)s and collection of global positioning system (GPS) datasets, 5) documenting the degree of noxious weed infestations via preparation and submittal of a comprehensive electronic database, 6) preparation and submittal of invoices for payment of services, and 7) providing proof of application, such as GPS spray tracks, physical or digital maps, etc. will be required. title: USACE Basis of Design J&A for Interior Finishes - Notice of Intent
description: USACE requests a class justification and approval (J&A) for other than full and open competition to allow Contracting Officers to issue solicitations for construction contracts where �brand name or equal� references are necessary to effectively communicate interior color and finish selections. The estimated cost for this class J&A is $230 million, covering projects from Fiscal Year (FY) 27 through FY29. 10 U.S.C � 3204(a)(1) as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Part 6 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Class Deviation 2026-O0017, Revision 1. DFARS 206.103-170(c) states �Notwithstanding FAR 6.103-1(d), in accordance with section 888(a) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (Pub. L. 114-328), the justification and approval addressed in FAR 6.104 is required in order to use brand name or equal descriptions.� This class J&A alleviates the need to execute an individual J&A on a contract-by-contract basis when using such descriptions or specifications in accordance with applicable FAR and DFARS sections. The plans and specifications issued as part of a construction solicitation may include brand name or equal references for architectural finishes that shall be regarded as establishing a standard of quality and shall not be construed as limiting competition to the identified brand. The Contractor may, at its option, use any product that, in the judgement of the Contracting Officer, is equal to that named in the specifications, unless otherwise specifically provided in the contract. This Notice of Intent is not applicable to any single project but covers all construction projects for which the designation of finish colors and/or aesthetic is reasonably anticipated. The funding for these projects encompasses all funds USACE obligates for construction including the Civil Works Mission, the Military Construction Mission and all projects executed by USACE contracting in support of International and Interagency Missions. The individual projects this J&A covers will be solicited across the USACE districts, using whatever acquisition method is deemed most appropriate for the requirement. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the agency. The submission must be received no later 1600 PM Eastern Time on 9 October 2026 to Michael.D.Hutchens@usace.army.mil. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL.

This is a SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. It is for information and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation announcement nor a request for proposals or quotes and does not obligate the� Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals, nor will any award be made to any parties responding to the sources sought announcement. The purpose of this Sources Sought Announcement is to conduct market research to locate interested, experienced and potential qualified constructions firms capable of completing this project. Firm must identify their socio-economic status for NAICS Code 238220, Plumbing, Heating, and Airconditioning Contractors. The appropriate North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 238220 with the applicable business size of $19.0 million. The project cost range is between $500,000.00 to $1,000,000.00 GENERAL SCOPE OF WORK: Executive Summary 1. This contract is for CONSTRUCTION services for the work required address identified deficiencies within 6 clean supply rooms at Buildings 51, 52, and 53 at the St. Louis Medical Center, Jefferson Barracks. The construction contract drawings and specifications were created by an ArchitectEngineer consultant designer (DESIGN-AIRE ENGINEERING, INC.). 2. Description: All associated construction work will correct HVAC deficiencies to ensure these rooms have proper air pressure relationships, temperature, humidity and air exchanges per the outlined directives. Scope of Work covers 6 rooms in the following buildings: B51 Mental Health (3Rooms), B52 Spinal Cord Injury (2 Rooms), and B53 Community Living Center (1 Room). The project includes correction in part or in whole of the following FCAs: 78420 and 78392. VASTLHCS' improvements will reduce energy consumption and green-house gas emission pursuant to Executive Orders 13423 and 13514. a. Building 51 i. Room 1A119 ii. Room 1E137 iii. Room 1W155A b. Building 52 i. Room 1N104 ii. Room 1S16 c. Building 53 i. Room 1N90 For all three buildings, the general scope of work will include: 1. Demolition and removal of existing electrical and mechanical components. 2. Basic architectural scope such as drywall work and suspended ceiling grid modifications. 3. Installation of new HVAC mechanical components, per the specifications and construction documents parameters. 3. Note: Contractor to abide by all work & requirements set in the final release for construction project drawings and specifications. The complete set of contract documents, which includes drawings and specifications, detail the complete scope of work for this project. 4. Project shall conform to all Records Management and Privacy Language END OF SCOPE OF WORK. The Government will in no way be bound to this information if any solicitation is issued.� If interested in this opportunity, please provide Capability Statement via email. The submission is limited to 10 pages which shall include the following information: 1) Offeror's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, and DUNS number; 2) Offeror's interest in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued; 3) Offeror's capability to perform a contract of this magnitude and complexity and comparable work performed within the past 5 years - brief description of the project, customer name, timeliness of performance, customer satisfaction, and dollar value of the project) - provide at least 1 no more than 3 examples; 4) Offeror's CVE certification if a Veteran owned business; 5) Please provide Socio-economic status for NAICS code 238220, Plumbing, Heating, and Airconditioning Contractors, and provide percentage of self-performed labor your company can perform for this type of project; 6) Offeror's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential; 7) Offeror's Bonding Capability in the form of a letter from Surety providing bonding level per contract and aggregate.
