title: D--Replacement of NWQL's Wastewater Treatment Monitor
description: Replacement of US Geological Survey (USGS), National Water Quality Laboratory's (NWQL) Wastewater Treatment Monitoring Computer System THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB). NO FORMAL SOLICITATION IS BEING REQUESTED UNDER THIS NOTICE. This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes to identify parties having an interest in and resources to support this requirement for replacement of wastewater SCADA computerized control system and software package using Inductive Automation or equivalent software that replicates the functionality of the current SCADA control system with modern, reliable hardware and software while minimizing operational downtime for the US Geological Survey (USGS), National Water Quality Laboratory (NWQL). The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The Government will review the information requested in this announcement based on the responses to this sources sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses or procured through full and open competition. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services) and the size standard is $34.0 million. The following is a brief description of services that are required to be performed: A. Introduction: The US Geological Survey (USGS), National Water Quality Laboratory (NWQL) has a requirement for replacement of wastewater SCADA computerized control system and software package using Inductive Automation or equivalent software Inductive Automation or equivalent software that replicates the functionality of the current SCADA control system with modern, reliable hardware and software while minimizing operational downtime. B. Background: The USGS, NWQL operates a laboratory wastewater and treated ion exchange system. The Safety, Health, and Environmental (SHE) team relies on a computer-based supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) control system to assess discharge performance and maintain environmental compliance. The current system, installed in the mid 2000s, is aging and at risk of failure, which could result in operational shutdown of the laboratory. C. Scope of Work The Contractor shall provide all labor, software, programming, configuration, installation, testing, and documentation required to replace the existing wastewater SCADA control system. D. Technical Requirements: The Contractor shall provide the following: a. Installation, configuration and programming of Ignition Perspective HMI software b. Convert the existing Genesis32 software monitoring screens to Ignition Perspective and integrate logic, alarms and parameter settings. c. Integration of the Ignition Perspective software with the existing Allen Bradley PLC proprietary logic programing owned by others such that integration of the new software does not violate existing intellectual property ownership d. The new Ignition Perspective software will communicate with existing sensors, AB controllers, and treatment system components through the existing proprietary logic developed by others. e. System testing, commissioning, and acceptance verification f. Providing system documentation and operator training E. Functional Requirements: The new system shall: a. Seamless functionality with existing AB PLC proprietary logic programing own by others. b. Replicate and update current monitoring screens and functionality c. Interface with all existing sensors, PLCs, and control hardware d. Accurately measure, display, and record key wastewater parameters e. Provide alarm logic and notifications equivalent to the current system f. Automatically log discharge data for compliance records F. Installation Requirements: The Contractor shall: a. Coordinate installation to minimize downtime b. Ensure all work meets electrical and environmental safety standards c. Perform system cutover in a manner that maintains wastewater compliance capability (End of brief description of Services) If your organization has the potential ability to meet this requirement, please provide the following information to the Contracting Officer: 1. A tailored capability statement describing detailed information in providing wastewater SCADA computerized control system services outlined above. 2. The firm shall specify that they are either: 2.1 A small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, etc. and Or 2.2 Other than small business under the NAICS Code listed in the announcement. 2.3 The firm shall provide a point of contact name and e-mail information, and SAM.gov (Unique Entity ID (UEI) and must be registered and active in System for Award Management (SAM). All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary � the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Materials submitted to the Government for review will not be returned. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotations (RFQ) or Invitation for Bid (IFB). The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses received under this announcement. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated. In order to be responsive to this Notice, a firm shall provide the appropriate documentation for consideration by October 9, 2026 at 2:30 p.m. Mountain Daylight Time (MDT). Responses that do not comply with these procedures will not be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Inquiries will only be accepted by e-mail to Lisa Williams at lisa_williams@ios.doi.gov.

Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. title: BPA FOR VIRUS ISOLATION AND PCR ANALYSIS
description: Virus isolation and molecular RNA analysis services for U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Upper Midwest Water Science Center Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for Virus isolation and molecular RNA analysis services for U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Upper Midwest Water Science Center. This RFQ seeks to establish a single award open market Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) in accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR part 12.201-1(3)-Blanket Purchase Agreement for an experienced laboratory to provide virus isolation and molecular RNA analysis to support U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), Upper Midwest Water Science Center. The anticipated period of performance is October 19, 2026 through October 18, 2030. The BPA will have a maximum ordering limit in the amount of $300,000.00 for a four year term. 2. This Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) is established under the authority of FAR Part 12 acquisition of commercial products and commercial services. The BPA provides a simplified method for meeting anticipated recurring needs for the supplies or services described herein. All purchases made under this BPA shall comply with the procedures at RFO FAR 12.201 1(e)(3) governing establishment of commercial BPAs, and RFO FAR 12.204(c)(1) governing commercial BPA orders. 3. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 and the FAR Overhaul deviations. 4. The solicitation is NOT a Small Business Set-Aside. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541380 (Testing Laboratories and Services) and the size standard is $19.0 million. 5. In accordance with FAR Provision 52.204-7 System for Award Management. (NOV 2024) (Deviation MAR 2026), Vendors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer or quotation in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Allow for processing time when registering in SAM. If the Offeror is not registered in SAM, it should register immediately after receiving this Solicitation. 6. Please download attached Solicitation 140G0226Q0186 for all BPA Clauses and Provisions and Attachments.

The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. title: SHI Replace Lead Glazed Bathtubs at United States Coast Guard Rio Bayamon Housing Base San Juan, Puerto Rico PNUM 24658602
description: SOURCES SOUGHT: THIS IS ONLY A SURVEY OF THE MARKET TO DETERMINE IF THERE ARE POTENTIAL CONTRACTORS THAT CAN SATISFY THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENT: SHI Replace Lead Glazed Bathtubs at United States Coast Guard Rio Bayamon Housing Base San Juan, Puerto Rico PNUM 24658602 Provide Design-Build services for the repair work required for SHI Replace Lead Glazed Bathtubs at United States Coast Guard Rio Bayamon Housing Base San Juan, PR. Perform the work according to this specification: Summary of Scope of Work The contractor shall conduct pre-construction asbestos containing materials and lead-based paint survey and testing on all materials affected by the work. Remove and replace with new 120 existing lead glazed bathtubs. Provide new steel glazed bathtubs that are free of lead and secure them against walls. Upon completion of work, the contractor shall provide certification showing area to be clear of any asbestos containing materials or lead based paint. Properly coordinate generated waste from lead glazed bathtubs A. Any waste generated shall be properly characterized and shall be recycled or be disposed of in accordance with RCRA requirements. Dispose of all waste in accordance with federal/PuertoRico/local laws. B. All wastes to include paint chips, debris and whole bathtubs must be labeled correctly and hazardous waste manifests prepared and signed for any hazardous waste. If not hazardous, ensure disposal goes to an approved landfill. The performance period of the design and construction phase will be a total of two hundred ninety (240) calendar days. The estimated value of this procurement is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The applicable North American Industry Class System (NAICS) code is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The small business size standard has an annual gross receipt of $25 million. Bid, Payment, and Performance Bonds are REQUIRED. The following are tentative dates for this project: Solicitation Issued: October 2026 Bid Opening: November 2026 Contract Performance Completion: July 2027 SAM: Interested parties should register in the System for Award Management (SAM) database as prescribed in FAR 4.203-1(b). SAM registration can be obtained by accessing the internet at www.sam.gov. USCG posts opportunity and award information to SAM. The U.S. Coast Guard is considering whether or not to set aside this acquisition for a HUBZone, Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Women Owned Small Business (WOSB). Please reference the above project number in all correspondence pertaining to this project. Your response MUST include the following: (a) a positive statement of intent to submit a bid/proposal for this solicitation as a prime contractor; (b) a statement identifying you are a certified small business designation; (c) evidence of experience with work similar in type and scope to include contract numbers, project titles, dollar amounts, points of contact, and telephone numbers; (d) evidence of bonding capability to the maximum magnitude of the project, to include both single and aggregate totals; (e) documentation verifying small business certification and socioeconomic category designation by SBA; (f) Unique Entity ID (UEI).
